methods.label: Use repeated inputs
methods.explanation:
The identity \(a\diamondsuit a=1\) suggests choosing repeated inputs so that an inner operation becomes \(1\). For any nonzero \(a\), setting \(b=c=a\) gives
\[
a\diamondsuit1
=a\diamondsuit(a\diamondsuit a)
=(a\diamondsuit a)a
=a.
\]
Now set \(c=b\), where \(a,b\ne0\). Then
\[
a=a\diamondsuit1
=a\diamondsuit(b\diamondsuit b)
=(a\diamondsuit b)b.
\]
Division by the nonzero number \(b\) shows that
\[
a\diamondsuit b=\frac ab.
\]
This rule satisfies both given identities: \(a/a=1\), and for nonzero inputs,
\[
\frac{a}{b/c}=\left(\frac ab\right)c.
\]
Using the given nesting identity, the required equation is therefore
\[
(2016\diamondsuit6)x=100,
\qquad 336x=100.
\]
Its unique solution is
\[
x=\frac{100}{336}=\frac{25}{84},
\]
which is positive and nonzero. Since \(25=5^2\) and \(84\) is not divisible by \(5\), this fraction is in lowest terms. Thus \(p+q=25+84=\boxed{109}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
